result.verdict: GP-215 arc-level cycles map cleanly and exhaustively to paper 5's ten verification operations: all 40 cycles receive a best-op assignment, 38 at high confidence and 2 at medium, with zero unmapped and zero forced low-confidence matches. The distribution is cross-substrate (ns, aqual, and neural all participate) and spans eight of the ten operations, with op5_anchor_proxy_requirement (12 cycles) and op2_controlling_claim_isolation (9 cycles) dominating — reflecting that the most common arc-level recovery move is either binding an abstract variable to a concrete readable proxy or isolating the load-bearing claim into a formal skeleton. Op1_eigenquestion_identification is the only operation with zero instances, suggesting GP-215 cycles rarely need to identify a single master question because the eigenquestion is already fixed by the substrate's proof target. The clean mapping, high confidence, and cross-substrate distribution strongly support the hypothesis: GP-215's arc-level cycles ARE paper 5's verification operations applied at arc scale — same move-shapes, different granularity. GP-215 is not a genuinely distinct layer; it is paper 5's framework instantiated one level up.

structural_answer: SAME FRAMEWORK AT DIFFERENT SCALE — 40/40 cycles map cleanly with high/medium confidence; 5 ops have cross-substrate spread. GP-215 is paper 5 ops applied at arc level.
